checklist.step: Define and maintain the annuity surveillance metric set
actions: Define the metric set with thresholds: replacement ratio by producer, share of sales to consumers aged 75 and over, premium above 50 percent of liquid net worth, sales funded from qualified plan rollovers, sales of the longest surrender-charge product, free-look cancellation rate and first-year surrender rate.
Set an amber and a red threshold for each metric against the book average, and record the rationale for the level chosen.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the metric set covers the Section 6.D duty to detect recommendations that are not in compliance.
Version and date the definition so a later quarter's results can be read against the thresholds in force at the time.
checklist.done: each metric has a written definition, amber and red thresholds, a recorded rationale and a dated version.

checklist.step: Produce the quarterly surveillance run
actions: Extract the quarter's issued Group Annuity contracts with producer NPN, state, product, premium, consumer age, replacement flag, funding source and commission paid.
Compute every metric at producer, agency, distributor, state and product level and load the results to the supervision dashboard.
Reconcile the contract count and premium to the policy administration issue register before publishing.
Publish a ranked exception list of every producer and distributor breaching an amber or red threshold.
checklist.done: all metrics are computed at five levels, reconciled to the issue register, and a ranked threshold-breach list is published.

checklist.step: Work every red-threshold breach to a conclusion
actions: Open a supervision issue for each red breach naming the producer or distributor, the metric, the value and the book average.
Pull five of that producer's cases from the quarter and read the profile, suitability review and disclosures end to end.
Conclude within 30 days of the surveillance run: explained by the producer's book, a training gap, or suspected unsuitable sales practice.
Escalate suspected unsuitable practice to the Producer Compliance Manager for conduct action the same week the conclusion is reached.
checklist.done: every red breach carries a five-case review and a written conclusion within 30 days, with conduct referral where practice is suspected.

checklist.step: Draw and document the quarterly sales sample
actions: Take 100 percent of replacement cases, 100 percent of consumers aged 75 and over, and 100 percent of cases from producers on an open conduct plan.
Take 40 further contracts by seeded random selection, spread so every state with in-quarter sales and every distributor is represented at least once.
Record seed, population size, stratum sizes and selection date on the sampling sheet.
Publish the sampled contract list to the reviewers before the case files are requested.
checklist.done: the sample covers all replacements, seniors and conduct-plan producers plus 40 seeded random contracts spanning every active state and distributor.

checklist.step: Review each sampled sale end to end against the four Model 275 duties
actions: For each sampled contract score the care duty (profile complete, product fits objectives, replacement comparison quantified), the disclosure duty (Appendix A and package delivered on time), the conflict duty (compensation described, no unexplained higher-paying choice) and the documentation duty (consumer-specific reasonable basis).
Score each duty pass, pass with observation, or fail, and write the evidence reference behind each score.
Refer every fail to the Compliance Manager the same day with a consumer-harm assessment.
Reviewers may not score their own prior decisions — reassign those cases within the desk.
checklist.done: every sampled contract carries a four-duty score with evidence references and same-day referral of every fail.

checklist.step: Run the producer conduct escalation ladder
actions: Apply the ladder: first finding coaching with a documented conversation; second finding a written corrective action plan with 100 percent pre-issue review of that producer's cases for two quarters; third finding suspension of annuity selling authority.
Record each step with date, the finding that triggered it and the manager who applied it on the producer record.
For suspension or termination, check whether the state requires a termination-for-cause notice to the department and file it within the state's deadline.
Review every producer on 100 percent pre-issue review monthly and record whether the enhanced review is actually happening.
checklist.done: every finding moves the producer one rung of the ladder with a dated record, and required department notices are filed within the state deadline.

checklist.step: Correlate complaints and early cancellations with the surveillance results
actions: Extract every annuity complaint and department of insurance inquiry received in the quarter with producer NPN, state, allegation type and outcome.
Extract free-look cancellations and first-year surrenders and match them to producer NPN.
Join both to the surveillance results and flag any producer appearing in complaints or early cancellations who did not breach a metric threshold — that gap means the metric set is missing something.
Feed proposed metric changes back to the Compliance Manager for the next definition version.
checklist.done: complaints and early cancellations are matched to producers and to the metric results, with metric-set gaps identified and fed back.

checklist.step: Oversee third-party distributors and any outsourced supervision
actions: Confirm each IMO, FMO, broker-dealer and TPA agreement carries the Section 6.D clauses: the insurer retains responsibility, the distributor supplies suitability and training records, and the insurer may audit.
Collect the quarterly attestation from each distributor covering training coverage, suitability review performance and complaint counts.
Audit at least the two largest distributors and any distributor with a red surveillance metric each year, on site or by file review.
Where the distributor performs suitability review under contract, re-perform 10 of their reviews and report the agreement rate.
checklist.done: every distributor has the required contract clauses and a current attestation, the largest two and any red-metric distributor are audited annually, and delegated reviews are re-performed.

checklist.step: Apply the securities and fiduciary safe harbour where it genuinely applies
actions: Identify sales made by registered representatives under a broker-dealer's Regulation Best Interest supervision, or by an adviser under a fiduciary standard, that may fall in the Model 275 safe harbour.
Obtain from the broker-dealer written confirmation that its supervision covers the transaction and that it applies comparable standards.
Confirm the safe harbour is claimed only where the comparable standard actually applied, and never for a fixed annuity sold outside the broker-dealer's supervision.
Record the basis on the contract record so an exam can see why our own review was scoped differently.
checklist.done: every safe-harbour claim is supported by written broker-dealer confirmation and a recorded basis on the contract.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly supervision report
actions: Within 30 days of quarter end publish the report: surveillance results and threshold breaches, sampling results by the four duties, producer conduct actions, complaint correlation and distributor oversight status.
Show the trend against the prior three quarters for each metric so a drift is visible.
List every open issue with owner and remediation date, and every issue overdue.
Circulate to the Head of Distribution, the Chief Risk Officer and the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is published within 30 days of quarter end with trends, open issues and named owners, and circulated to the three recipients.

checklist.step: Produce the annual senior management report on the supervision system
actions: By 31 March, compile the Section 6.D annual report for the prior calendar year covering the supervision system's design, the reviews performed, findings, corrective actions and system changes made.
State explicitly whether the system is reasonably designed to achieve compliance with the best-interest standard, and name any deficiency not yet remediated.
Have the Chief Risk Officer sign the report and record the date and the senior management forum at which it was received.
File the signed report and its supporting quarterly reports as one exam-ready pack.
checklist.done: a Chief Risk Officer signed annual report exists by 31 March with an explicit design conclusion, named deficiencies and a recorded receipt date.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the annuity Market Conduct Annual Statement data
actions: Assemble the prior calendar year annuity MCAS data by state: contracts issued, replacements, surrenders, complaints, lawsuits and producer counts.
Reconcile each state's figures to the policy administration issue register, the complaints log and the commission records before entry.
Submit through the NAIC MCAS application by the 30 April deadline for every state that calls the annuity blank, and retain the submission confirmation.
Answer state validation queries within the department's stated response window and record each answer.
checklist.done: annuity MCAS data is reconciled, submitted for every calling state by 30 April, with confirmations and query answers retained.

checklist.step: Decide and execute consumer remediation on systemic findings
actions: Where sampling shows the same failure across a producer's book or a distributor's channel, scope the full affected population rather than remediating only the sampled cases.
Agree the remedy with Regulatory Counsel: free-look extension, surrender charge waiver, rider charge refund, or rescission with full premium and interest.
Execute the remedy, write to every affected consumer, and track acceptance and payment to completion.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether the finding requires self-reporting to the affected state departments and record the decision either way.
checklist.done: every systemic finding has a full-population scope, an agreed remedy executed to payment, and a recorded self-report decision.

checklist.step: Feed supervision findings back into the controls that caused them
actions: Map each finding to the upstream control that should have prevented it: profile validation edits, the suitability test set, the disclosure package definition or the training gate.
Raise a control change request against the owning team with a due date, rather than only fixing the individual case.
Verify in the following quarter's surveillance that the changed control moved the metric.
Close the finding only when the control change is live and the metric has moved.
checklist.done: each finding is mapped to an upstream control with a change request, and closes only after the control is live and the metric has moved.

checklist.step: Retain the supervision evidence for the full retention period
actions: Archive the surveillance extracts, sampling workpapers, producer conduct files, distributor audit reports, quarterly reports and the signed annual report under Annuity Supervision.
Apply the 6-year retention label from the report date, and the longer label where a state adoption requires it.
Confirm retrieval by quarter, by state, by producer NPN and by distributor.
Apply legal hold on any supervision record connected to an open market conduct exam, department inquiry or litigation.
checklist.done: the full supervision record set is archived, labelled for at least 6 years, retrievable four ways and held where a matter is open.

testing.step: Build the population of supervision activity for the quarter
actions: Extract every surveillance run, threshold breach, supervision issue, sampled case review, producer conduct action and distributor attestation recorded for the quarter.
Extract the underlying issued-contract population for the same quarter from the policy administration issue register as the independent denominator.
Include the prior quarter's open issues so unremediated items are visible.
Record extract date, filters and row counts on the workpaper cover sheet.
testing.done: the supervision activity set and the independent contract denominator are both extracted, including carried-forward open issues.

testing.step: Reconcile the surveillance denominator to the issued-contract register
actions: Compare the contract count, premium and state spread used in the surveillance run to the policy administration issue register for the same quarter.
Investigate any state, product or distributor missing from the surveillance run — an excluded channel means the metrics understate the risk.
Confirm third-party distributor sales are inside the denominator and not reported only through the distributor's own attestation.
Sign and lock the reconciliation before testing the metrics themselves.
testing.done: the surveillance denominator ties to the issue register with every state, product and distributor present, and the reconciliation is signed.

testing.step: Recompute the surveillance metrics from source data
actions: Independently recompute the replacement ratio, senior sales share, premium-to-liquid-net-worth breach count, free-look cancellation rate and first-year surrender rate from the raw contract, profile and commission tables.
Compare each recomputed figure to the published dashboard value and investigate any variance above 0.5 percentage points.
Check the thresholds applied were the version in force during the quarter, not the current version.
Attach the recomputation script output and the variance table to the workpaper.
testing.done: every metric is independently recomputed, variances above 0.5 points are explained, and the correct threshold version is confirmed.

testing.step: Test that every red threshold breach was actually worked
actions: List every red breach from the recomputed metrics and match it to a supervision issue in the GRC platform.
Check each issue has the five-case review, a written conclusion and a conclusion date within 30 days of the surveillance run.
Treat a breach with no issue, or an issue closed with no five-case review, as a supervision control failure rather than a documentation gap.
Read three closed conclusions in full and assess whether the evidence supports the conclusion reached.
testing.done: every red breach has a matching issue with a five-case review and a conclusion inside 30 days, and three conclusions are evidence-tested.

testing.step: Re-perform the quarterly sampling to confirm it was complete and unbiased
actions: Redraw the sample from the locked population using the recorded seed and confirm it reproduces the same contract list.
Confirm the mandatory strata were taken at 100 percent: replacements, consumers aged 75 and over, and conduct-plan producers.
Check every state with in-quarter sales and every distributor is represented, and list any that were not.
Flag any evidence of sample substitution — a case swapped out after selection is a control failure.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the seed, mandatory strata are complete, coverage gaps are listed and no substitution occurred.

testing.step: Re-perform the four-duty scoring on a subset of the reviewed cases
actions: Take 15 cases already scored by the Suitability Desk and score them independently on care, disclosure, conflict and documentation without reading the desk's scores.
Compare and compute the agreement rate; any case the desk passed that audit fails is reported individually with the evidence.
Check no reviewer scored a case they had previously decided, using the reviewer names on both records.
Attach both score sheets side by side in the workpaper.
testing.done: 15 cases are independently re-scored with a computed agreement rate, disagreements reported individually and reviewer independence confirmed.

testing.step: Test the producer conduct ladder was applied on time
actions: List every producer with a finding in the quarter and read the conduct record for the ladder step applied and its date.
Confirm a second finding produced a corrective action plan with 100 percent pre-issue review, and check that the enhanced review actually occurred on that producer's subsequent cases.
Confirm suspensions took effect in the Broker & Agent Portal and that no case was created by a suspended producer afterwards.
Check any termination for cause was notified to the state department within its deadline and the notice is on file.
testing.done: every finding produced the correct dated ladder step, enhanced reviews are evidenced on later cases, and terminations are notified with proof.

testing.step: Test third-party distributor oversight and the annual report
actions: Pull each active distributor agreement and confirm the Section 6.D clauses on retained responsibility, record supply and audit rights are present and executed.
Confirm a current quarterly attestation exists for every distributor and that missing attestations triggered the new-business withholding.
Confirm the two largest distributors and any red-metric distributor were audited in the last 12 months, and read one audit report end to end.
For the annual senior management report, confirm it was signed by the Chief Risk Officer on or before 31 March and that every deficiency named in it traces to an open or closed GRC issue.
testing.done: every distributor agreement, attestation and required audit is evidenced, and the annual report is signed by 31 March with deficiencies traceable to issues.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one audit issue per supervision failure naming the quarter, the metric or process, and the consumer or regulatory exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: metric not computed, channel excluded from the denominator, breach not worked, sampling incomplete, ladder step skipped, distributor unaudited, report late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and require the Head of Compliance to respond in writing to each issue within 15 business days.
